hand_ups.record_correction_verbatim: CORRECTED PIN RULE (three parts + the 0-hex clause) for docs/PLAN_CORRECTIONS.md:1542-1543, which still says a short pin is 'accepted but reported loudly' (FALSE for 1-11 hex). Correct wording: The pin's enforced policy (_same_digest: width = min(len(a), len(b), 64); True iff width >= 12 and a[:width] == b[:width]; _pin_is_overlong and the PIN_EMPTY state are both checked BEFORE the comparison): (1) an entry that exists but carries NO value — exactly 0 hex — is the DISTINCT state `PIN_EMPTY`: REFUSED before any comparison, reported as `pin empty` (lowercase), never a mismatch and with NO `PIN ABBREVIATED` note; (2) 1-11 hex is REFUSED as a mismatch: _same_digest cannot compare it at all under the width >= 12 floor, so it is fail-closed, never a 'reduced strength' match, and carries NO `PIN ABBREVIATED` note; (3) 12-63 hex that matches is accepted at reduced strength and reported loudly (`PIN ABBREVIATED` run note + `REDUCED STRENGTH` stage clause); (4) exactly 64 hex that matches is accepted silently; (5) more than 64 hex is REFUSED as `PIN OVERLONG` before the comparison, even though _same_digest would return True on its first 64 characters. 'Shorter than 12 -> mismatch' is imprecise at 0; 'short pin accepted but reported loudly' is false for 1-11.
